panels.title: Timeline

panels.description:
## cpusys(Autotracing)

Detects abnormal spikes in system CPU usage (`sys`, kernel space) on physical hosts.  
When triggered, it automatically generates flame graphs and provides process-level context for root cause analysis.

Helps identify and resolve application jitter and latency issues caused by abnormal system load.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions (ANY of the following):**
- `sys` CPU usage > 50%
- `sys` CPU usage fluctuation > 30% within 1 second
panels.title: cpusys

panels.description:
## softirq(Event)

Detects excessively long softirq disabled duration in the kernel.  
Outputs kernel call stack and process context information for analysis.

Helps identify and resolve system stalls, network latency, and scheduling delays.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Softirq disabled duration > 100 ms
panels.title: softirq

panels.description:
## netdev down (Event)

Detects network device link status changes.

Identifies both physical link failures and administrative (software-triggered) link-down events on network interfaces.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Network interface down event detected (physical layer down or administrative down)

  OR tracer_name:netdev_bonding_lacp
)

panels.title: netdev down

panels.description:
## cpuidle (Autotracing)

Detects abnormal decreases in container CPU idle rate, automatically generates flame graphs and provides process context information.

Addresses abnormal container CPU usage and helps analyze process hotspots.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions (ANY of the following):**
- `sys` CPU usage > 45%  
- `user` CPU usage > 75% AND fluctuation > 30% within 10 seconds  
- `usage` CPU usage > 90% AND fluctuation > 30% within 10 seconds
panels.title: cpuidle

panels.description:
## container loadavg (Autotracing)

Detects sudden increases in container load average.  
Automatically captures call stack information of D-state processes within the container.

Helps identify and resolve issues caused by spikes in D-state processes, resource contention, or long-held locks.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- D-state process detected in container
panels.title: container loadavg

panels.description:
## net rx latency (Event)

Detects latency events along the network receive path (driver → protocol stack → user space).

Helps identify and resolve application timeouts and jitter caused by receive-side latency.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions (ANY of the following):**
- NIC → driver receive latency > 5 ms  
- NIC → protocol stack receive latency > 10 ms  
- NIC → user-space copy latency > 115 ms  

**Latency location filters (`where`):**
- `TO_NETIF_RCV`  
- `TO_TCPV4_RCV`  
- `TO_USER_COPY`  

> Note: Most events are attributed to `TO_USER_COPY`, indicating delays caused by user-space read operations exceeding the threshold.
panels.title: net rx latency

panels.description:
## softlockup (Event)

Detects softlockup events and provides target process and kernel stack information.

Helps locate and resolve system softlockup issues.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Softlockup event detected
panels.title: softlockup

panels.description:
## ras (Event)

Detects hardware faults across CPU, memory, PCIe, and other subsystems.

Enables timely detection of hardware failures to minimize impact on applications.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Hardware error event detected
panels.title: ras

panels.description:
## iotracing (Autotracing)

Detects abnormal disk I/O latency on physical hosts.  
Automatically captures related process, container, disk, and file-level context.

Helps identify and resolve application latency and system performance jitter caused by I/O saturation or sudden spikes in disk access.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions (ANY of the following):**

**1. HDD / SATA SSD:**
- `io.util` > 90% sustained for > 2 seconds  
- 2-second average I/O latency > 100 ms  

**2. NVMe SSD:**
- `io.util` > 90% AND I/O bandwidth exceeds:
  - Read > 2000 MB/s **OR**
  - Write > 1500 MB/s  
- 2-second average I/O latency > 100 ms
panels.title: iotracing

panels.description:
## oom (Event)

Detects Out-Of-Memory (OOM) events on the host or within containers.

Focuses on memory exhaustion issues and provides detailed fault snapshots for analysis.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- OOM event detected on host or container
panels.title: oom

panels.description:
## waitrate (Autotracing)

Detects abnormal increases in container wait rate based on statistical anomaly detection.  
Continuously analyzes historical wait rate behavior and identifies significant deviations.

Helps identify performance degradation caused by resource contention, scheduling delays, or blocking operations.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- For each container, compute `mean` and `std` of wait rate over the past 30 minutes  
- Alert is triggered when:
  - `waitrate > mean + std × factor`

**Service levels:**
- Level 0: factor = 30  
- Level 1: factor = 40  
- Level 2: factor = 60
panels.title: waitrate

## hungtask (Event)

Detects hung task events and outputs all processes in D-state along with their stack traces.

Captures transient scenarios with large numbers of D-state processes and preserves the fault context for analysis.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Hung task event detected
panels.title: hungtask

panels.description:
## reclaim (Event)

Detects direct memory reclaim events, recording reclaim duration along with process and container context.

Helps identify and resolve application stalls caused by memory pressure.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Within a 1-second sampling window, cumulative time a process spends in `sys` state > 900 ms  
  *(Note: due to non-preemptible kernel execution, observed duration may exceed 1 second)*
panels.title: reclaim
dropwatch

panels.description:
## memburst (Autotracing)

Detects sudden bursts in memory allocation on physical hosts.  
Automatically captures process-level memory usage context.

Helps identify scenarios with rapid memory growth that may trigger direct reclaim or OOM conditions.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Memory usage doubles within the last 5 minutes AND current anonymous memory usage on the host ≥ 70%
panels.title: memburst

panels.description:
## TX queue timeout (Event)

Detects network interface transmit queue timeout events.

Helps identify and locate hardware or driver issues in the NIC transmit queue.

### Threshold Definition

**Trigger conditions:**
- Transmit queue timeout event detected
